newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Irish foes to meet in South Africa.
newsitem.headline: Irish foes to meet in South Africa.

text.p: Nine Northern Ireland political parties, including Sinn Fein and the Ulster Unionist Party, will meet South African negotiators near Cape Town from Friday, a government minister said.

But Minister of Constitutional Affairs Mohammed Valli Moosa told a news conference arrangements were in place to ensure that the Ulster Unionist Party (UUP) and the Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) did not have to meet or see the Sinn Fein delegation.
"This is not a continuation or part of negotiations on the Northern Ireland question. It is about discussing the South African transition," Valli Moosa said.

He said South Africa had been asked to host the meeting to share its own experience of peaceful transition from the racial conflict that raged before 1990 to the democracy implemented through non-racial elections in 1994.

"It is not about mediation of any kind...It is also not about South Africa advising on the Northern Ireland question. We do not feel that we have the expertise or knowledge to do that," said Valli Moosa, who was a key African National Congress negotiator in talks with the former white government.
He said the Sinn Fein delegation would be headed by chief negotiator Martin McGuinness and the UUP by David Trimble.
